name: Houston Gas Pipeline (HPL) System / Edinburg Lateral

values.OtherEnglishNames: Edinburg Extension; HPL Border Crossing Project
values.EndLocation: US-Mexico border at the Rio Grande, near Reynosa

researcher_notes: Houston Pipe Line Company LP, an Energy Transfer unit, built 23 miles of 24-inch intrastate pipe from its existing Edinburg Lateral in Hidalgo County, Texas to the Rio Grande near Reynosa. Design capacity is about 140 million cubic feet per day. The EIA August 2026 release (Historical Projects sheet, Excel row 795) lists it as Edinburg Lateral, Expansion, Completed, in service 2015-06-08, 23 mi, 24 in, 140 MMcf/d, FERC docket CP14-13. The FERC environmental assessment notice in the Federal Register of 26 December 2013 states the 23 miles, 24-inch size, 140 million cubic feet per day and that the pipeline is intrastate. An Oil and Gas Journal story from March 2014 reports the presidential permit approval. Not an existing row: P0203 is the whole 3,800 mile HPL system with endpoints 'Multiple'; this is its own expansion project (about 37 km, above the 25 km threshold). Capacity is the new line's design capacity; EIA lists it as additional capacity. The cost was not found. The pipeline stops at the border; the Mexican side belongs to Pemex and is not included. The 2013 Federal Register notice for CP14-13 only names the border crossing, so it supports the owner and the location but not the length. No official route file was found, so no route is staged. Tier high: three sources, but the EIA and Federal Register may share the FERC filing as an origin.
